title: The documented sink-retirement gate is structurally blind to the NudgeStreamer buffer and returns a false all-clear
fingerprintBasis: sha256(src/StableYieldAccumulator.sol:setNudgeAddress:keyed-external-state-orphaned-by-local-setter-documented-migration-has-no-drain-step-retirement-gate-blind)  [entryPoint null -> legacy hash form, byte-identical to pre-entryPoint findings]
description: From 'retirement permanently destroys up to 30 days of nudge donations' to 'retirement certifies clean while ~30 days of nudge donations sit outside the gate's field of view, recoverable only by an unprompted manual cross-contract intervention that the runbook gives the operator no reason to perform'.
impact: FALSE ASSURANCE, not destruction of funds. The retirement gate `require(IERC20(USDC).balanceOf(OLD_BATCH_MINTER) == 0, "old contract still holds USDC")` certifies clean while ~30 days of nudge donations (converging to donationRate x duration) sit in the NudgeStreamer, outside the gate's field of view, with every AUTOMATIC delivery route dead.
attackPath: No attacker. Owner-footgun path on a documented procedure.
1. The streamer buffer is keyed on the pair (nudge, rewardToken).

2. Owner performs the DOCUMENTED migration: registerStream(B_new, USDC, d), then setNudgeAddress(B_new). The ops NatSpec (:82-90) prescribes registering the NEW pair first and says nothing about draining the OLD one.
3. The old (B_old, USDC) buffer is now orphaned: new claims fund the new pair, and the old buffer's only drain is the old sink calling pullPendingStream itself.
4. If B_old is being retired — the usual reason to repoint — that drain never runs and the float is stranded in the dead end described at L-03.
recommendation: PRIMARY (unchanged, and still the highest-value deliverable of this audit): extend the retirement gate at ReplaceBatchNFTMinter.s.sol:486 and MigrateBatchNFTMinter.s.sol:500 from `require(IERC20(USDC).balanceOf(OLD_BATCH_MINTER) == 0)` to additionally assert `pendingStream(oldSink, token) == 0` AND the streamer's buffer for that pair == 0. As written the assertion is a false assurance.

SECONDARY (new, and only correctly specifiable under the corrected rationale): document the manual recovery route in the ops runbook — a 1-wei collectNudge or an owner registerStream pushes the buffer to the retired sink, and rescueERC20 recovers it from there, callable even while paused. Note that de-whitelisting the token first REMOVES the owner's registerStream lever, so drain BEFORE de-whitelisting.
TERTIARY: add a step 0 to the SYA ops-ordering NatSpec (:82-90) — drain the old (sink, token) stream before repointing. Unchanged from the classifier's original recommendation and still correct.
law3Ruling: IN SCOPE and unchanged as a non-obvious owner footgun. The surprise test is met decisively: an operator runs the documented retirement, the script's own safety assertion passes, and ~30 days of donations are outstanding in a contract the gate never looks at, with every automatic delivery route now dead. A competent, non-malicious owner would be surprised. Law 3 requires this be reported at honest severity — and honest severity here is Low.

poc.provenance: AUDIT-AUTHORED, UNTRACKED UPSTREAM. Not part of the project's own test suite: the only test file tracked at f704130 is test/StableYieldAccumulator.t.sol. Never cite this as a project test.
poc.retentionMandate: Retain the R1/R2/R3 refutation tests. They are the record of what is NOT true (the buffer IS recoverable via _settle push + rescueERC20) and must not be trimmed as redundant. Filename retains its 'M-02' origin from the withdrawn Medium raise; the finding is a LOW.

pocProved: The gate is blind and returns a false all-clear — STRONGER than I filed it. Even an operator who runs the documented drain and recovers 496.2 USDC via rescueERC20 still gets `require(IERC20(USDC).balanceOf(OLD_BATCH_MINTER) == 0)` passing while 4,108 USDC sits in the streamer (test_M02_01).
The outstanding amount converges to donationRate x duration: observed 14,982,961,180 vs 15,000,000,000 expected, ~30 days of donations, with the gate still reading zero (test_M02_04).

All three severing mechanisms independently kill the DESIGNED automatic delivery route — pause, de-whitelist, zero-streamer (test_M02_02a/02b/02c). The classifier's original Low rationale ('batchMint is permissionless so anyone can drain it indefinitely') is therefore FALSE at retirement, which is exactly when it matters.
NudgeStreamer has no rescue/sweep/withdraw surface — 10 signatures probed — and pullPendingStream is msg.sender-keyed, with 4 non-recipient callers confirmed as no-ops (test_M02_03).

The buffer is UN-REDIRECTABLE: registering the replacement sink's stream leaves the old buffer keyed to the retired pair. Value cannot be moved to the new sink; it can only be pushed to the old one and rescued from there.
pocRefuted: 'Permanently unrecoverable / no rescue path from any address' — FALSE. _settle PUSHES (NudgeStreamer.sol:186).
registerStream pushes the buffer to the retired sink; rescueERC20 then recovers it — 4,108,708,527 recovered (test_M02_R1).
A 1-wei collectNudge by ANY address achieves the same push (test_M02_R2).

De-whitelist retirement blocks the owner's registerStream lever, since registerStream re-checks isNudgeToken (NudgeStreamer.sol:112-114) — leaving the outsider 1-wei route as the remaining path (test_M02_R3).

rationaleCorrection.note: The label returns to where the classifier had it, but this is NOT a vindication of the classifier's reasoning, and the finding must not be written up as though nothing happened. Three positions have now been held, and the third is the correct one:
rationaleCorrection.classifierOriginal: Low, because 'batchMint is permissionless and its step-3.5 flush loop runs unconditionally, so any caller can drain the orphan indefinitely.' REFUTED by test_M02_02a/02b/02c — every automatic route dies at retirement. Right label, wrong reason.
rationaleCorrection.myRaise: Medium, because the buffer is permanently unrecoverable. REFUTED by test_M02_R1/R2 — _settle pushes. Wrong label, wrong reason.
rationaleCorrection.correctPosition: Low, because although every AUTOMATIC delivery route dies at retirement, a manual push (registerStream by the owner, or a 1-wei collectNudge by anyone) still delivers the buffer to the retired sink, where rescueERC20 recovers it in full. The defect is the FALSE ASSURANCE — the gate certifies clean while the value is outstanding and while every automatic route to it is dead — not the destruction of funds.
rationaleCorrection.whyThisMatters: The corrected rationale is what makes the recommendation actionable and correctly scoped. Under the classifier's reasoning there is nothing much to fix, because organic batchMint demand supposedly handles it. Under mine, the fix would have been framed as preventing catastrophic loss. Under the correct reading, the fix is precise: extend the gate, and document the manual recovery route so the operator knows it exists. That is a Low-severity fix for a Low-severity defect — but it is a fix that neither prior position would have specified correctly.

escalationTriggers.condition: the old sink can ever reach a state where rescueERC20 is unavailable -- ownership renounced, or the sink self-destructed/upgraded away
escalationTriggers.evidenceAtHEAD: NOT evidenced at f704130; retirement as scripted leaves the contract intact and owner-controlled.

escalationTriggers.condition: a retirement procedure is adopted that revokes the shared owner's control of the retired sink as part of decommissioning
escalationTriggers.basis: that removes the rescueERC20 endpoint this Low depends on

resolvedSwingFactors.resolution: sink retirement IS documented ops practice -- STANDS. Untouched by the _settle refutation.

'NudgeStreamer has no rescue function' is TRUE (10 signatures probed) but DOES NOT imply 'the buffer is unrecoverable'. _settle PUSHES (NudgeStreamer.sol:186); an owner registerStream, or a 1-wei collectNudge by ANY address, pushes the buffer to the retired sink where rescueERC20 recovers it in full (4,108,708,527 recovered, test_M02_R1/R2). THAT INFERENCE IS THE TRAP THIS RUN FELL INTO. A future run must not re-derive it.

De-whitelisting the token FIRST removes the owner's registerStream lever (registerStream re-checks isNudgeToken, NudgeStreamer.sol:112-114), leaving only the outsider 1-wei collectNudge route (test_M02_R3). DRAIN BEFORE DE-WHITELISTING.

manualRecoveryRoute: 1-wei collectNudge by any address, OR owner registerStream, pushes the buffer to the retired sink; rescueERC20 then recovers it in full, callable even while paused. MUST be stated explicitly in the write-up -- it is the operator's remedy and the reason this is Low.

validity.note: Retaining a PoC on a Low is unusual and correct here: two of the three positions taken on this finding were wrong, and the PoC is what settles it.
